Shop & Craft

Woodworking

Furniture and small-shop woodworking — cutting boards, coasters, and built furniture.

Woodworking projects ranging from small functional pieces like cutting boards and coasters to multiple styles of selves.I started woodworking when I was about 12 taking an industrial arts class in middle school. I’ve always enjoyed working with my hands and creating things that are functional and beautiful so I immediately took an interest. Through high school and college I continued to learn and teach others what I have learned through TA-ing classes in high school and being a shop monitor in college.

I believe woodworking is becoming a lost art and I am trying to do my part to keep all that knowledge alive and in use. My favorite woods to work with are walnut due to the dark color but also the variation of color you can bring out of the wood. The top of my desk shown on the metalworking page is walnut. Aromatic cedar is a close second, of course for the wonderful smell but also the stunning streaks of red and white that you can see in the shelves I’ve made.

Projects

Hand-Carved Tool Handles

A set of hand-carved and hafted tool handles — a few full-size axes, two hammers, and two hatchets — each shaped from raw wood blanks and monogrammed.

Shelves & Wall Storage

Wall-mounted storage pieces — a hand-built wine rack, a rope-suspended hanging shelf system, and an aromatic cedar bookshelf.

End-Grain Cutting Boards

Four cutting boards — an end-grain brick-pattern design with a monogram, a board with an inlaid grape cluster made from wine stained barrel oak, a striped walnut/maple/mahogany design, and a maple and purple heart board with an inlaid heart.

Miscellaneous Projects

Smaller shop projects — wood slice coasters, a set of parquet trivets, and a climbing hangboard.
